chapter: Early New Orleans and Plaquemine years
title: Living by the graveyard; learning back home; teaching Sidney Williams
summary: Love lived by a canal and graveyard, fell sick, returned to Plaquemine to his mother and taught Sidney Williams trumpet.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: Well at that time, Peter Buchhosh was playing guitar with Charlie DeVoges. He was a professor like mine. That's all down there on that canal down there. I was living there, right by the graveyard, I was living there with my cousin, little bit of fella, you know, call myself and they can plant him on there.
Is that the Whitney Avenue canal or Whitney Avenue, that canal you're talking about or what avenue?

Yeah. That's on New Nez, on New Nez Street. Oh yeah. That's big canal there. And a graveyard right by the, I lived in that last house, right by the graveyard. I used to go in the early that night, I was scared, you know. Scared of ghosts. I was a little boy, I remember that this as well, and I got sick. And they sent me, my cousin sent me back to Plackham, to my mother, you see. I got around there and got me up a nut, little man, started playing around there. And I learned a boy how to play, they called him Sidney Williams. He made a nice trumpet player, but he's dead now.
